sections.title: SRN PLAINS
sections.text: AN UPPER-LEVEL LOW WILL DIG SEWD ACROSS NWRN MEXICO TODAY. AHEAD OF THE SYSTEM...DIFFLUENT SOUTH SOUTHWESTERLY FLOW WILL BE IN PLACE ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS AS SEVERAL SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS MOVE NNEWD ACROSS THE REGION. AT THE SFC...A BROAD CORRIDOR OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WITH MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL BE IN PLACE FROM THE TX COASTAL PLAINS NNWWD ACROSS THE TX HILL COUNTRY AND INTO THE RED RIVER VALLEY. ALTHOUGH WEAK FORCING FOR ASCENT IS FORECAST ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR TODAY...ISOLATED TO SCATTERED STORMS MAY DEVELOP ALONG CORRIDORS OF ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE. AS THE UPPER-LEVEL LOW MOVES INTO NCNTRL MEXICO TONIGHT...LARGE-SCALE ASCENT WILL INCREASE ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS RESULTING IN A GRADUAL EXPANSION OF CONVECTIVE COVERAGE ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR. SQUALL-LINE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS EVENING FROM SOUTH TX NEWD ACROSS THE TX COASTAL PLAINS AS A WELL-FOCUSED 45 TO 60 KT LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS AND MOVES TO THE MIDDLE TX COAST. NAM FORECAST SOUNDINGS AT 03Z FROM NEAR SAN ANTONIO TO VICTORIA SHOW SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S F...MLCAPE FROM 1500 TO 2000 J/KG AND 0-6 KM SHEAR NEAR 50 KT. sections.title: TX/OK AND VICINITY
sections.text: A LARGE CLUSTER OF CONVECTION -- INCLUDING EMBEDDED BOWS AND LOCAL SUPERCELL STRUCTURES -- CONTINUES MOVING EWD ACROSS CENTRAL AND ERN TX AND ADJACENT SRN OK. THE STORMS ARE MOVING THROUGH AN AREA OF MODEST INSTABILITY BEING AIDED BY CONTINUED NWD ADVECTION OF INCREASINGLY RICH GULF MOISTURE. WHILE A GRADUAL DECREASE IN SEVERE RISK ACCOMPANYING THIS CONVECTION IS EXPECTED AS STORMS MOVE INTO THE ARKLATEX REGION /WHERE INSTABILITY DIMINISHES/...LOCAL SEVERE RISK -- INCLUDING POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES -- WILL LIKELY CONTINUE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON HOURS AS STORMS PERSIST ON THE SRN/SWRN FLANK OF THE MCS. LATER THIS AFTERNOON...ISOLATED STORMS ARE FORECAST TO REDEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF NWRN TX/SWRN OK...WHERE DIURNAL HEATING OF A MORE MARGINALLY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER YIELDS 500 TO 1000 J/KG MIXED-LAYER CAPE. LARGE HAIL AND LOCAL WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS. FINALLY...THE ADVANCE OF THE UPPER LOW ACROSS NRN MEXICO AND ASSOCIATED INCREASE IN ASCENT ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL AND SRN TX SHOULD RESULT IN A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN CONVECTION OVER ROUGHLY THE ERN HALF OF TX. WHILE FLOW ALOFT WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY SLY/MERIDIONAL AND WEAK SHORT-WAV

THE CHANGES MADE TO THE PRIOR OUTLOOK INCLUDE 1) THE REMOVAL OF THE SLIGHT-RISK EQUIVALENT PROBABILITIES ACROSS OK AND A SIZABLE PORTION OF N-CNTRL TX DUE PRIMARILY TO STABILIZATION FROM THE EXTENSIVE MCS DURING THE MIDDAY TIMEFRAME. 2) ADJUSTED TORNADO PROBABILITIES HIGHER ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE ARKLATEX REGION WHERE SURFACE PRESSURE FALLS ARE MAXIMIZED ALONG WITH A DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER CO-LOCATED WITH ADEQUATE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR FOR STORM ROTATION. 3) NARROWED A CORRIDOR FOR POSSIBLE STRONG TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT OVER WRN N-CNTRL TX WHERE SOME RECENT STORM-SCALE GUIDANCE CONTINUES TO HINT AT STORMS DEVELOPING LATER THIS AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...TRENDED DOWNWARD WITH HAIL/WIND/TORNADO PROBABILITIES DUE TO REDUCED BUOYANCY/SHEAR THAN PREVIOUSLY OUTLOOKED. ..SMITH.. 03/08/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1035 AM CST TUE MAR 08 2016/
